items.title: Ella MOCN
items.text: Ella MOCN integrates your neutral host radio network with mobile operators. It is a Multi-Operator Core Network (MOCN) gateway: your radios connect to Ella MOCN, and Ella MOCN connects them to each operator's core.

items.title: Key features
items.text:
• Multi-Operator: Share one 4G and 5G radio network between several operators. Radios connect to Ella MOCN, and each operator sees a single base station.
  • 4G and 5G Compliant: Ella MOCN integrates with 4G and 5G networks following 3GPP standards. It has been validated with commercial radios, phones and cores.
  • User-Plane Aggregation: Optionally carry subscriber traffic through Ella MOCN's eBPF-based data plane, so Ella MOCN acts as a single point of contact for operators.
  • Lightweight: A single binary with an embedded UI, API and database. Install with snap, Docker or Kubernetes, or from source.
  • Single Sign-On: Users log in through an identity provider, such as Google, Microsoft or Okta, over OpenID Connect.
  • Easy to Operate: Manage operators and radios through a web interface or a RESTful API with an OpenAPI specification. Monitor every radio, MME and AMF, and each operator's traffic, with logs, metrics (Prometheus), traces (OTel) and profiles.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
Ella MOCN is a Multi-Operator Core Network (MOCN) gateway. It lets one neutral host radio network serve the subscribers of several mobile operators, with each operator keeping its own core network.

Neutral host architecture

items.title: What each side sees
items.text:
• Radios connect to Ella MOCN as if it were their core. They broadcast the networks of every operator they serve, and need no per-operator configuration.
  • Each operator sees Ella MOCN as a single base station. The operator provisions one node, however large the neutral host's network grows.

Adding an operator does not touch the radios, and adding a radio does not involve the operators.

When a phone connects, it picks one of the networks the radio broadcasts, and Ella MOCN sends its signalling to the operator that owns that network.

items.title: Mobility
items.text: When a phone moves between radios, the operator's core stays in charge of the handover, as it would with its own radios. Ella MOCN delivers the handover to the right radio, so phones keep their connection as they move through the neutral host's network. The core finds Ella MOCN by tracking area, so the neutral host's tracking areas must not be reused elsewhere in the operator's network.

items.title: Public warnings
items.text: The sharing operators agree on one of them to send public warnings, such as emergency alerts, for the whole shared network. Ella MOCN broadcasts that operator's warnings on every radio in the warning area, and does not broadcast warnings from the others. When a radio restarts, Ella MOCN tells that operator, so its warnings are sent to the radio again.

items.title: Security
items.text:
Info

To report a security vulnerability, please file a Private Security Report.

Security is one of Ella MOCN's core tenets. From the UI to the database, security is built into every layer of the system.

items.title: Authentication & Authorization
items.text:
Ella MOCN enforces authentication on API requests towards most endpoints. Two authentication methods are supported:

  • Session-based authentication. Users authenticate with email and password, or through single sign-on. A session cookie and a short-lived access token are issued. The login endpoint limits attempts per client address and per account.
  • API tokens. Per-user tokens that can expire and be revoked individually. A token has its user's role, but cannot create API tokens, change a password or manage users. Recommended for programmatic access.

items.title: Role-Based Access Control
items.text:
Every request is authorized against a role-based permission system with three built-in roles:

Role Scope Admin Full access to all resources and operations. Network Manager Read Only, plus creating, updating and deleting operators. Cannot manage users. Read Only Reads operators, radios and UE connections.

items.title: Secret Storage
items.text:
• User passwords are stored as one-way hashes. Verification uses constant-time comparison.
  • API token secrets are stored as one-way hashes. The raw token is returned only once at creation time and is never retrievable afterward.
  • Session tokens are cryptographically random values. Only a one-way hash is persisted.
  • JWT signing secret is a cryptographically random value generated once and stored in the database.

items.title: API and UI
items.text:
Ella MOCN uses TLS to secure its API and web interface. The TLS configuration is defined in the configuration file.

Ella MOCN supports TLS 1.2 and 1.3.

items.title: Operators
items.text: Ella MOCN can reach operator cores with IPsec tunnels. The tunnels are set up on the host, and Ella MOCN uses them to reach the operator's MMEs and AMFs, and its S-GWs and UPFs with user-plane aggregation. See Connect an Operator over IPsec.

items.title: Radios
items.text: Ella MOCN does not encrypt S1 and NG toward the radios, and does not check a radio's identity. Protect the link to the radios, for example with IPsec set up on the host or a private network.

items.title: Minimal Attack Surface
items.text:
Ella MOCN minimizes its attack surface through minimal packaging:

  • Container image. Built on a distroless base with no operating system layer, shell, or package manager. Only the strictly necessary runtime dependencies are included. Image size: under 100 MB.

items.title: Audit Logging
items.text: Ella MOCN writes security-relevant events, such as logins and changes to operators and users, to its log as audit events. Each records who did what, and when.

items.title: Single Sign-On
items.text:
Users can log in to the UI through the organization's identity provider instead of, or as well as, a password. Ella MOCN works with any OpenID Connect identity provider, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Ping Identity, Google or Keycloak. To set it up, see Configure Single Sign-On.

Login page with single sign-on

items.title: Password and single sign-on
items.text:
Password Single sign-on Credentials kept by Ella MOCN The identity provider, with its own policies, such as multi-factor authentication Role set by An Admin An Admin, or the highest role from the user's groups at the identity provider Session 30 days The session lifetime, 24 hours by default Access removed by Deleting the user in Ella MOCN, at once Removing the user at the identity provider, at the end of their session

Password login stays when single sign-on is on, and at least one Admin always keeps a password. An identity provider that is down or misconfigured cannot lock everyone out.

items.title: Matching users
items.text: A user is matched to their account at the identity provider, not to their email address, so a changed or reused email address does not give access to another user. The email address is used once, to link the account at its first login, only if the identity provider has verified it and the user has no password. A user with a password links from their profile. A provider that does not say whether email addresses are verified, such as Microsoft Entra ID, must be trusted explicitly: anyone who can set their email address there could take over the matching user. An account with no user in Ella MOCN gets one only from a group mapping, within the limit of 50 users.

items.title: Offboarding
items.text: Ella MOCN does not learn when someone is removed at the identity provider. Their session lasts until its lifetime ends, and their API tokens until deleted. A shorter session lifetime narrows that window, at the cost of logging in more often. To end access at once, offboard the user in Ella MOCN.

items.title: User-Plane Aggregation with eBPF
items.text: While signalling always goes through Ella MOCN, you can choose to have subscriber traffic go through Ella MOCN too. This is called user-plane aggregation.

items.title: Direct vs aggregated
items.text: User-plane aggregation

items.title: Direct
items.text: Each radio sends its traffic straight to the operator's network. The radios and the operator's network must reach each other, so every radio needs an address the operator can route to.

items.title: Aggregated
items.text: Ella MOCN carries the traffic between the radios and the operator's network. The operator sees only Ella MOCN's address, and the radios stay on the neutral host's private network. Subscriber traffic follows the same path as Ella MOCN's signalling to that operator, typically its IPsec tunnel. All of that operator's traffic then depends on Ella MOCN's capacity and availability.

items.title: How Ella MOCN forwards traffic
items.text: Ella MOCN uses eBPF to relay subscriber traffic between the radios and the operators' networks in the kernel. With Traffic Control, it puts its own tunnel endpoints in place of the radios' and the operators', so each side only ever sees Ella MOCN. It never touches the traffic inside the tunnels.

items.title: Back Up and Restore
items.text:
This guide backs up Ella MOCN's database while Ella MOCN runs, and restores it.

The backup holds user accounts and the single sign-on client secret. Store and transfer it encrypted.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Ella MOCN: installed, as in Install.

  • sqlite3: installed on the host.

    sudo apt install -y sqlite3

items.title: Back up
items.text:
SnapSourceDocker 
sudo sqlite3 /var/snap/ella-mocn/common/mocn.db ".backup mocn-backup.db"

Back up the database at db.path in the configuration file:

sqlite3 /var/lib/mocn/mocn.db ".backup mocn-backup.db"

In the directory of docker-compose.yaml, back up the database in the ella-mocn-data volume:

sudo sqlite3 "$(docker volume inspect -f '{{.Mountpoint}}' ella-mocn_ella-mocn-data)/mocn.db" ".backup mocn-backup.db"

items.title: Restore
items.text:
SnapSourceDocker

  1. Stop Ella MOCN:

    sudo snap stop ella-mocn.mocnd

  2. Replace the database with the backup:

    sudo rm -f /var/snap/ella-mocn/common/mocn.db-wal /var/snap/ella-mocn/common/mocn.db-shm
sudo cp mocn-backup.db /var/snap/ella-mocn/common/mocn.db

  3. Start Ella MOCN:

    sudo snap start ella-mocn.mocnd
  1. Stop Ella MOCN.

  2. Replace the database with the backup:

    rm -f /var/lib/mocn/mocn.db-wal /var/lib/mocn/mocn.db-shm
cp mocn-backup.db /var/lib/mocn/mocn.db

  3. Start Ella MOCN.

In the directory of docker-compose.yaml:

  1. Stop Ella MOCN:

    docker compose stop ella-mocn

  2. Replace the database with the backup:

    D="$(docker volume inspect -f '{{.Mountpoint}}' ella-mocn_ella-mocn-data)"
sudo rm -f "$D/mocn.db-wal" "$D/mocn.db-shm"
sudo cp mocn-backup.db "$D/mocn.db"

  3. Start Ella MOCN:

    docker compose start ella-mocn

items.title: Configure Single Sign-On
items.text: This guide lets users log in to the Ella MOCN UI through an OpenID Connect identity provider.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Ella MOCN: reached by users over HTTPS, at a URL with no path.
  • Identity provider: an OpenID Connect provider, reachable from Ella MOCN over HTTPS.
  • Ella MOCN account: an Admin that logs in with a password.

The examples use these values:

Value Role https://mocn.example.com Ella MOCN's external URL https://mocn.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback Redirect URL: the external URL followed by /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback https://mocn.example.com/login Post-logout redirect URL: the external URL followed by /login

items.title: 1. Register Ella MOCN at the identity provider
items.text:
KeycloakOther providers

In the realm users log in to:

  1. Go to Clients and click Create client.
  2. Set Client type to OpenID Connect and Client ID to mocn. Click Next.
  3. Turn on Client authentication. Keep Standard flow checked. Click Next.
  4. Set Valid redirect URIs to the redirect URL and Valid post logout redirect URIs to the post-logout redirect URL. Click Save.
  5. In the client's Credentials tab, copy the Client Secret.

In Users, turn on Email verified for each user.

  1. Register a web application, or confidential client, with the redirect URL and the post-logout redirect URL.
  2. Create a client secret for it.
  3. Allow the openid, email and profile scopes.

If the provider does not send email_verified, turn on Trust email addresses from this provider in step 2.

items.title: 2. Configure Ella MOCN
items.text:
In the UI, go to Single Sign-On.

  1. In URLs, click Edit, set External URL to https://mocn.example.com, and click Update. Check that the Redirect URL and Post-logout redirect URL are the ones registered in step 1.

  2. In Provider, click Edit, set these fields, and click Update:

    Field Value Display name The name on the login button, such as Keycloak Issuer URL Keycloak: https://<keycloak-host>/realms/<realm>. Otherwise, from the provider. CA certificate The PEM CA certificate of the identity provider, only if a private CA signs its certificate Client ID Keycloak: mocn. Otherwise, from the provider. Client secret The secret from step 1 Scopes openid email profile Session lifetime 24 hours Trust email addresses from this provider Off, unless the provider does not send email_verified

items.title: 3. Enable single sign-on
items.text: On the Single Sign-On page, turn on Enabled.

items.title: 4. Log in
items.text:
1. Give a user access: create their user, or map their groups to a role.
  2. In a private browser window, open https://mocn.example.com, and click Log in with your display name.
  3. Log in at the identity provider. Ella MOCN opens.

items.title: Connect a Radio
items.text:
This guide connects a 4G radio (eNB) or a 5G radio (gNB) to Ella MOCN, which connects it to every operator whose PLMN it broadcasts.

  1. Set the radio's core address:
    • for a 4G radio (eNB), set the MME address to an address of the Ella MOCN host that ran.signalling.address listens on (all IPv4 addresses (0.0.0.0) by default), and the port to ran.signalling.s1_port (36412 by default);
    • for a 5G radio (gNB), set the AMF address to an address of the Ella MOCN host that ran.signalling.address listens on (all IPv4 addresses (0.0.0.0) by default), and the port to ran.signalling.ng_port (38412 by default).
  2. Broadcast at least one PLMN of an operator that has MMEs (4G) or AMFs (5G).
  3. In Radios, check that the radio's status is Up.

items.title: Connect an Operator
items.text:
This guide connects Ella MOCN to an operator's core, through its MMEs for 4G, its AMFs for 5G, or both.

  1. In Operators, click Create, then enter the operator's name and PLMNs.
  2. Connect the operator's MME, the operator's AMF, or both.
  3. Connect a radio that broadcasts one of the operator's PLMNs.

items.title: Connect the Operator's MME
items.text:
1. Open the operator. Next to 4G Gateway Identity (Global eNB ID), click the edit icon, turn on Set a Global eNB ID, enter the Global eNB ID the operator assigned to you and click Save.
  2. In Core Network Nodes, click Add Core Node, choose MME (4G), enter the MME's addresses and click Add.
  3. Ask the operator to accept your Global eNB ID, the TAIs of your 4G radios and the name Ella MOCN on its MMEs.
  4. Once a 4G radio is connected, check that the MME's status is Up.

items.title: Connect the Operator's AMF
items.text:
1. Open the operator. Next to 5G Gateway Identity (Global gNB ID), click the edit icon, turn on Set a Global gNB ID, enter the Global gNB ID the operator assigned to you and click Save.
  2. In Core Network Nodes, click Add Core Node, choose AMF (5G), enter the AMF's addresses and click Add.
  3. Ask the operator to accept your Global gNB ID, the TAIs of your 5G radios and the name Ella MOCN on its AMFs.
  4. Once a 5G radio is connected, check that the AMF's status is Up.

To carry the operator's subscriber traffic through Ella MOCN, enable user-plane aggregation.

items.title: Connect an Operator over IPsec
items.text:
This guide connects Ella MOCN to an operator's security gateway through a route-based IPsec tunnel, using strongSwan.

HostKubernetes

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Host: Ubuntu Server 26.04, with a certificate and private key signed by a CA the operator trusts.
  • Operator's security gateway: its address and its CA certificate.
  • Operator's networks: the networks that hold the operator's MMEs, AMFs, S-GWs and UPFs.

items.title: 1. Install strongSwan
items.text:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y strongswan-swanctl charon-systemd

items.title: 2. Create the xfrm Interface
items.text:
Create one xfrm interface per operator. Set its MTU to the MTU of the interface that reaches the operator's security gateway, minus 100 bytes for IPsec.

Create /etc/systemd/network/50-xfrm-opa.netdev:

[NetDev]
Name=xfrm-opa
Kind=xfrm
MTUBytes=1400

[Xfrm]
InterfaceId=1
Independent=yes

Create /etc/systemd/network/50-xfrm-opa.network, with Ella MOCN's address toward the operator and a route to the operator's networks from that address:

[Match]
Name=xfrm-opa

[Network]
Address=192.0.2.10/32

[Route]
Destination=10.45.0.0/16
PreferredSource=192.0.2.10

Apply the configuration:

sudo networkctl reload

Check that the operator's networks are routed through the xfrm interface:

ip route get 10.45.0.1

items.title: 3. Configure the Tunnel
items.text:
Install the host's certificate and key, and the operator's CA certificate:

sudo install -m 644 mocn.pem /etc/swanctl/x509/
sudo install -m 600 mocn.key /etc/swanctl/private/
sudo install -m 644 operator-a-ca.pem /etc/swanctl/x509ca/

Create /etc/swanctl/conf.d/operator-a.conf:

connections {
    operator-a {
        version = 2
        local_addrs = 198.51.100.10
        remote_addrs = 203.0.113.1
        local {
            auth = pubkey
            certs = mocn.pem
        }
        remote {
            auth = pubkey
            id = "CN=segw.operator-a.example"
        }
        if_id_in = 1
        if_id_out = 1
        children {
            operator-a {
                local_ts = 192.0.2.10/32
                remote_ts = 10.45.0.0/16
                start_action = start
                dpd_action = restart
            }
        }
    }
}
  • local_addrs and remote_addrs: the host's address and the operator's security gateway.
  • remote.id: the identity in the operator's security gateway certificate.
  • local_ts: Ella MOCN's address toward the operator.
  • remote_ts: the operator's networks.
  • if_id_in and if_id_out: the InterfaceId of the xfrm interface.

items.title: 4. Start the Tunnel
items.text:
sudo swanctl --load-all

Check that the tunnel is up:

sudo swanctl --list-sas

Then connect the operator. Its MMEs and AMFs are reached through the tunnel.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Ella MOCN: installed with the Helm chart, in a namespace that allows privileged pods.
  • Operator's security gateway: its address, its identity and the credentials it accepts.
  • Operator's networks: the networks that hold the operator's MMEs, AMFs, S-GWs and UPFs.

items.title: 1. Create the swanctl Configuration
items.text:
Create operator-a.conf, with an if_id_in and if_id_out per operator:

connections {
    operator-a {
        version = 2
        remote_addrs = 203.0.113.1
        local {
            auth = psk
            id = mocn.example
        }
        remote {
            auth = psk
            id = segw.operator-a.example
        }
        if_id_in = 1
        if_id_out = 1
        children {
            operator-a {
                local_ts = 192.0.2.10/32
                remote_ts = 10.45.0.0/16
                start_action = start
                dpd_action = restart
            }
        }
    }
}
secrets {
    ike-operator-a {
        id-1 = mocn.example
        id-2 = segw.operator-a.example
        secret = "<pre-shared key>"
    }
}

To authenticate with certificates instead, add them to the Secret below and reference them by their path in /etc/swanctl/conf.d.

items.title: 2. Create the Secret
items.text: kubectl -n ella create secret generic ella-mocn-ipsec --from-file=operator-a.conf

items.title: 3. Turn On IPsec
items.text:
1. In values.yaml, add one xfrm interface per operator. Set id to the connection's if_id_in and if_id_out, address to Ella MOCN's address toward the operator, mtu to the MTU toward the operator's security gateway minus 100, and routes to the operator's networks:

    ipsec:
  enabled: true
  secretName: ella-mocn-ipsec
  interfaces:
    - name: xfrm-opa
      id: 1
      address: 192.0.2.10/32
      mtu: 1400
      routes:
        - 10.45.0.0/16

  2. Upgrade the chart:

    helm upgrade ella-mocn oci://ghcr.io/ellanetworks/charts/ella-mocn --version <version> --namespace ella -f values.yaml

  3. Check that the tunnel is up:

    kubectl -n ella exec ella-mocn-0 -c ipsec -- swanctl --list-sas

Then connect the operator. Its MMEs and AMFs are reached through the tunnel.

items.title: Enable User-Plane Aggregation
items.text: This guide carries an operator's subscriber traffic through Ella MOCN, so the operator sees Ella MOCN's addresses instead of the radios'.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Operator: connected over IPsec, as in Connect an Operator over IPsec, with its S-GWs and UPFs in the networks routed through the tunnel.
  • User-plane interface: the interface of the Ella MOCN host that radios' user traffic arrives on.

items.title: Prepare the Host
Turn It On in Ella MOCN
items.text:
HostKubernetes

  1. With the snap, connect the network-control and mount-observe interfaces:

    sudo snap connect ella-mocn:network-control
sudo snap connect ella-mocn:mount-observe

  2. In the configuration file, set ran.user_plane.enabled to true, and set ran.user_plane.name to the interface radios' user traffic arrives on:

    ran:
  user_plane:
    enabled: true
    name: eth1

  3. Restart Ella MOCN.

  1. In values.yaml, set ran.address to Ella MOCN's address on the radios' network, and turn on userPlane.enabled:

    ran:
  address: 192.168.252.7/24
  networkAttachment:
    master: eth1
userPlane:
  enabled: true

  2. Upgrade the chart:

    helm upgrade ella-mocn oci://ghcr.io/ellanetworks/charts/ella-mocn --version <version> --namespace ella -f values.yaml

  3. Wait for the rollout:

    kubectl -n ella rollout status statefulset/ella-mocn

items.title: Turn It On for an Operator
items.text:
1. In Operators, open the operator.
  2. Next to User-Plane Aggregation, click the edit icon.
  3. Turn on User-plane aggregation and click Save.

items.title: Check the Operator's User Plane
items.text:
1. Check that Status in User Plane is Ready, and that Interface is the operator's xfrm interface.
  2. Ask the operator to accept the Addresses shown in User Plane on its MMEs, AMFs and gateways.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Choose one of the installation methods below.

Snap (Recommended)SourceDockerKubernetes

Install the Ella MOCN snap:

sudo snap install ella-mocn

Configure Ella MOCN:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-mocn/common/mocn.yaml

Start Ella MOCN:

sudo snap start --enable ella-mocn.mocnd

Install the required dependencies:

sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc

Clone the Ella MOCN repository:

git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/mocn.git
cd mocn

Build the frontend:

npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui

Build Ella MOCN:

go build -o mocn -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/mocn/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/mocn

Configure Ella MOCN:

vim mocn.yaml

Start Ella MOCN:

./mocn --config mocn.yaml

Create a new directory:

mkdir ella-mocn
cd ella-mocn

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml
configs:
  ella_mocn_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/mocn.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5030
      ran:
        signalling:
          address: 0.0.0.0
          s1_port: 36412
          ng_port: 38412

services:
  ella-mocn:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-mocn:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_mocn_config
        target: /mocn.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/mocn --config /mocn.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - ella-mocn-data:/data

volumes:
  ella-mocn-data:

Start the Ella MOCN container:

docker compose up -d

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster meets the Kubernetes requirements.

Create values.yaml. To give Ella MOCN an S1 and NG address on the radios' network, set address to that address and master to the host interface that connects to your radios:

ran:
  address: 192.168.252.7/24
  networkAttachment:
    master: eth1

To expose S1 and NG through a Service on the pod network instead, set the Service type:

ran:
  service:
    type: LoadBalancer

Deploy Ella MOCN:

helm install ella-mocn oci://ghcr.io/ellanetworks/charts/ella-mocn --version 0.0.1 --namespace ella --create-namespace -f values.yaml

Open the UI and API on your machine:

kubectl -n ella port-forward service/ella-mocn 5030:5030

The UI and API are at http://localhost:5030. See the chart reference for all values.

Ella MOCN's UI and API are at http://<host-ip>:5030. Open the UI and create the first user.

See the configuration reference for all options.

items.title: Manage Single Sign-On Users
items.text: This guide manages the users who log in through single sign-on. Configure single sign-on first.

items.title: Give a user access
items.text:
Create a user so that they can log in through the identity provider.

  1. In the UI, go to Users and click Create. Set:
    • Email: the user's email address at the identity provider
    • Password: off
    • Role: the user's role
  2. Click Create.

items.title: Map groups to roles
items.text: Map groups at the identity provider to roles so that their members get a role, and a user, when they log in.

items.title: 1. Send groups to Ella MOCN
items.text:
KeycloakOther providers
  1. Go to Clients, open the mocn client, and open the Client scopes tab.
  2. Click mocn-dedicated, then Configure a new mapper, or Add mapper > By configuration, then Group Membership.
  3. Set Name and Token Claim Name to groups. Turn off Full group path. Keep Add to ID token on.
  4. Click Save.

Configure the provider to send the user's groups in a claim, such as groups, as a list of group names or IDs.

items.title: 2. Map the groups in Ella MOCN
items.text:
1. Go to Single Sign-On and, in Roles from groups, click Edit.
  2. Set Groups claim to groups.
  3. Click Add group for each group, and set the group and its role.
  4. Click Update.

items.title: Link a user who has a password
items.text:
Link a user who has a password to their account at the identity provider.

  1. Log in to Ella MOCN with the password.
  2. Go to Profile and click Link display name account.
  3. Log in at the identity provider.

items.title: Unlink a user
items.text:
Unlink a user from their account at the identity provider.

  1. Go to Users and open the user.
  2. In Account, click Unlink, then Unlink.

items.title: Offboard a user
items.text:
Offboard a user to end their access to Ella MOCN.

  1. Remove or disable the user at the identity provider.
  2. In Ella MOCN, go to Users, open the user, and click Delete. This also deletes their API tokens.

To keep the user instead, open the user and:

  1. In Account, click Unlink, then Unlink.
  2. Click Remove Password, then Remove, if they have one.
  3. In API Tokens, delete each token.

items.title: Upgrade
items.text: This guide upgrades Ella MOCN to a new release.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Ella MOCN: installed, as in Install.
  • Target release: its version, such as v0.0.2.

items.title: 1. Upgrade
items.text:
SnapSourceDockerKubernetes

Refresh the snap:

sudo snap refresh ella-mocn

In the Ella MOCN repository, check out the target release:

git fetch --tags
git checkout <version>

Build the frontend:

npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui

Build Ella MOCN:

go build -o mocn -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/mocn/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/mocn

Stop Ella MOCN, then start it:

./mocn --config mocn.yaml

In the directory of docker-compose.yaml, pull the new image and restart the container:

docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

  1. Upgrade the chart:

    helm upgrade ella-mocn oci://ghcr.io/ellanetworks/charts/ella-mocn --version <version> --namespace ella -f values.yaml

  2. Wait for the rollout:

    kubectl -n ella rollout status statefulset/ella-mocn

items.text: Check the running version in the UI's top bar.

items.title: Reference
items.text:
This section provides reference material for Ella MOCN, from configuration options to the API and metrics.

  • API
  • Configuration File

  • Observability
  • Performance
  • System Requirements
  • 3GPP Compliance

items.title: 3GPP Compliance
items.text:
Ella MOCN implements 3GPP-standard interfaces for signalling.

Note

Open an issue if you notice a 3GPP-compliance gap or require a new capability for a production deployment.

items.title: S1AP (TS 36.413)
items.text:
• Management. S1 Setup, configuration updates, Reset, Error Indication, overload.
  • UE-associated signalling. Relayed between the radio and the MME, handover included.
  • Paging.
  • Warning message transmission.

items.title: NGAP (TS 38.413)
items.text:
• Interface management. NG Setup, configuration updates, NG Reset, Error Indication, AMF Status Indication, overload.
  • UE-associated signalling. Relayed between the radio and the AMF, handover included.
  • Paging.
  • Warning message transmission.

items.title: GTP-U (TS 29.281)
items.text: • User plane. Relayed between the radios and the operators' gateways, with user-plane aggregation.

items.title: Configuration File
items.text:
Ella MOCN is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella MOCN with the --config flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected. Changes take effect on restart.

The operators and radios are not in this file: they are in the database, and set with the UI or the API.

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
• logging (object, optional): The logging configuration.
    • level (string, optional): The log level: debug, info, warn, or error. Default info.
  • db (object): The database configuration.
    • path (string): The path to the SQLite database file.
  • api (object, optional): The HTTP API and UI.
    • address (string, optional): The IP address to listen on. Default 0.0.0.0.
    • port (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default 5030.
    • tls (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS, TLS 1.2 or later. Default: plain HTTP.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM private key.
  • ran (object, optional): The radios.
    • signalling (object, optional): The S1 and NG listeners that radios connect to.
      • address (string, optional): The IP address to listen on. Default 0.0.0.0.
      • s1_port (int, optional): The SCTP port of S1. Default 36412.
      • ng_port (int, optional): The SCTP port of NG. Default 38412.
    • user_plane (object, optional): The user plane towards the radios.
      • enabled (boolean, optional): Allow user-plane aggregation. When true, Ella MOCN sets net.ipv4.ip_forward and net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding to 1 at startup and needs the capabilities in the system requirements. When false, every operator uses the direct user plane. Default false.
      • name (string): The network interface that radios' user traffic arrives on. Ella MOCN's address is its first global IPv4 address, or else its first global IPv6 address. Either name or address must be set when enabled is true, not both.
      • address (string): Ella MOCN's user-plane address towards the radios. A unicast address of an interface of the host. Either name or address must be set when enabled is true, not both.
  • telemetry (object, optional): The traces.
    • enabled (boolean, optional): Export traces. Default false.
    • otlp_endpoint (string): The host:port of an OTLP/gRPC collector, over plain gRPC. Required when enabled is true.

With the snap, the configuration file is /var/snap/ella-mocn/common/mocn.yaml.

items.title: Example
items.text:
logging:
  level: info
db:
  path: /var/lib/mocn/mocn.db
api:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 5030
  tls:
    cert: /etc/mocn/api.pem
    key: /etc/mocn/api.key
ran:
  signalling:
    address: 0.0.0.0
    s1_port: 36412
    ng_port: 38412
  user_plane:
    enabled: true
    name: eth1
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  otlp_endpoint: localhost:4317

items.title: Observability
items.text: Ella MOCN supports four observability pillars: Logs, Metrics, Traces and Profiles.

items.title: Logs
items.text:
Ella MOCN writes its logs to standard output, one JSON object per line, at the level of logging.level in the configuration file: debug, info, warn or error.

Field Description ts Time of the event. level debug, info, warn or error. msg What happened. trace_id Trace ID of the span the event happened in, as 32 hex digits. Absent outside a span. span_id Span ID of the span the event happened in, as 16 hex digits. Absent outside a span. trace_flags W3C trace flags of that span, as 2 hex digits: 01 when sampled. Absent outside a span.

Other fields depend on the event.

items.title: Audit events
items.text:
Audit events are logs at level info with msg set to audit event.

Field Description action What was done, such as auth_login, auth_oidc_login or create_operator. actor Email of the user who did it. Empty when unknown. ip Address the request came from. details What was done, in words.

With user-plane aggregation:

Metric Type Labels Description ellamocn_user_plane_enabled Gauge 1 when ran.user_plane.enabled is true in the configuration file, 0 otherwise. ellamocn_user_plane_datapath_loaded Gauge 1 while the user-plane eBPF program is loaded, 0 otherwise. ellamocn_user_plane_state Gauge operator, state (ready, unavailable, off) 1 for the operator's current user-plane state, 0 for the other states. ellamocn_user_plane_unavailable Gauge operator, reason (not_connected, no_route, route_mismatch, no_address, interface_error, too_many_operators) 1 for the reason while the state is unavailable, 0 otherwise. ellamocn_user_plane_tunnels Gauge operator, direction GTP-U tunnels relayed. ellamocn_user_plane_tunnel_setups_total Counter operator, direction GTP-U tunnels set up. ellamocn_user_plane_tunnel_setup_failures_total Counter operator, interface (s1, ng), procedure, reason (user_plane_unavailable, no_route, route_mismatch, no_address, no_teid, too_many_paths, invalid_address, unknown_endpoint, other) Procedures whose user-plane transport could not be relayed. The UE is released, or the handover or path switch is rejected. ellamocn_user_plane_packets_total Counter operator, radio, direction G-PDUs relayed. End Marker and Tunnel Status messages are not counted. ellamocn_user_plane_bytes_total Counter operator, radio, direction Octets of the T-PDUs of the G-PDUs relayed: the inner IP packet, without the GTP-U header and extension headers. ellamocn_user_plane_dropped_packets_total Counter operator, path (fast, slow), reason GTP-U messages dropped. ellamocn_user_plane_slow_path_packets_total Counter reason Packets on user-plane interfaces that the fast path left to the kernel. ellamocn_user_plane_slow_path_relayed_total Counter operator, direction G-PDUs, End Markers and Tunnel Status messages relayed by the slow path. ellamocn_user_plane_error_indications_total Counter origin, result GTP-U Error Indications. ellamocn_user_plane_peer_up Gauge operator, side (radio, core), peer 0 once 3 Echo Requests in a row, sent every 60 s, go unanswered, 3 to 4 minutes after the peer stops answering. 1 otherwise. items.text:

items.text: Span Kind Description {method} {route} Server A request to the API, except /api/v1/livez, /api/v1/readyz, /api/v1/metrics and /api/v1/pprof/. items.title: Performance
items.text:
This reference document contains performance test results of Ella MOCN's datapath with user-plane aggregation, and of its signalling.

On a 16-vCPU virtual machine, Ella MOCN forwards 15 Gbps of subscriber traffic at 0% loss using about 3 vCPUs, adds under 0.1 ms of round-trip latency, and uses about 480 MiB of memory with 100,000 sessions. On a 20-core host, it relays 17,000 4G attaches or 11,000 5G registrations per second with user-plane aggregation.

items.title: Throughput
items.text:
The following table outlines Ella MOCN's user-plane throughput at 0% loss, in millions of packets per second (Mpps) and gigabits per second (Gbps), for subscriber IP packets of 46, 494 and 1456 bytes:

Table 1. User-plane throughput at 0% loss

Network Direction Throughput (Mpps) Throughput (Gbps) 46 B 494 B 1456 B 46 B 494 B 1456 B 4GUplink1.951.871.290.727.4115.0 Downlink1.641.921.380.607.6016.1 5GUplink1.761.361.200.655.3714.0 Downlink1.851.381.320.685.4615.3

The packet size represents only the IP packet for the subscribers and ignores Ethernet and GTP-U encapsulation.

All packets through Ella MOCN were relayed by the eBPF fast path: ellamocn_user_plane_slow_path_packets_total and ellamocn_user_plane_dropped_packets_total stayed at 0.

The value represents the round-trip time from a radio to the operator's S-GW and back.

The following table outlines the memory of the user plane by number of sessions, with one E-RAB and two GTP-U tunnels per session, on a host with 16 vCPUs:

items.title: Methodology
items.text:
We performed performance tests with Ella MOCN on Google Cloud, with three virtual machines in the same zone, of the following specifications:

  • Machine type: n2-standard-16 (16 vCPUs, 64 GB RAM)
  • OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-1017-gcp
  • NICs: 2 x gVNIC, 4 receive and 4 transmit queues each, MTU 1500
  • Networks: one for the radios and one for the operator

The Ella MOCN host had ran.user_plane.enabled set to true, the forward chain policy of nftables set to drop, its NIC interrupts spread over all vCPUs, and the nohz=off kernel parameter.

The tests used mocnperf, in the perf/ directory of the Ella MOCN repository: fake eNBs and a fake MME (4G), or fake gNBs and a fake AMF (5G), set up the sessions through Ella MOCN, a generator sent GTP-U from AF_PACKET sockets, and an XDP program counted the packets received.

Test parameters:

  • Sessions: 1024, one E-RAB each
  • Radios: 64, each at its own address
  • S-GWs: 16 addresses
  • Search: highest rate at 0% loss (RFC 2544), binary search with 5-second trials and 2% resolution
  • Confirmation: 10 seconds at 0% loss
  • Runs: 1

Latency test parameters:

  • Probes: 1000 per round, one every 10 ms
  • Rounds: 5 through Ella MOCN and 5 direct, alternating, median
  • Packet size: 84 B

items.title: Procedure Rate and Latency
items.text:
The following table outlines the highest rate of procedures Ella MOCN relayed, with 160 procedures in flight, and the time each took:

Table 6. Signalling procedure rate and latency

Procedure User-plane aggregation Rate (/s) p50 (ms) p99 (ms) 4G attach Off 43,981 2.27 3.74 4G attach On 17,102 6.18 9.23 5G registration Off 28,214 2.20 3.64 5G registration On 11,763 4.06 8.63 5G PDU session establishment Off 28,214 2.05 3.47 5G PDU session establishment On 11,763 6.72 10.97 4G paging 87,961 1.76 3.77 5G paging 103,679 1.55 3.15

The time of a 4G attach or 5G registration runs from the radio's Initial UE Message to the core's Initial Context Setup Request. The time of a PDU session establishment runs from the gNB's Uplink NAS Transport to the AMF's PDU Session Resource Setup Request. The time of a paging runs from the core's Paging to its arrival at every radio in the paging area. In 5G, each UE registers, then establishes one PDU session.

items.text:
The following table outlines the memory of 100,000 connected UEs, with user-plane aggregation:

Table 7. Signalling memory with 100,000 connected UEs

Procedure Connection rate (/s) Memory per UE 4G attach 20,783 4.7 KB 5G registration and PDU session establishment 12,463 5.2 KB

Memory per UE is the process RSS growth from 0 to 100,000 connected UEs, divided by 100,000, and includes the simulated radios and cores. eBPF map memory is in the datapath memory.

items.title: Methodology
items.text:
We performed signalling tests on one host, with the following specifications:

  • CPU: Intel Core Ultra 7 265K, 20 cores
  • Memory: 64 GB
  • OS: Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0

The tests used the end-to-end benchmarks in internal/e2ebench of the Ella MOCN repository: Ella MOCN, simulated eNBs or gNBs, and simulated MMEs or AMFs of two operators ran in one process on the host, over SCTP. Each UE was released after its procedure.

Test parameters:

  • Procedures in flight: 160, one radio per procedure
  • Paging area: 8 radios
  • Duration: 5 seconds per run
  • Runs: 3, median
  • Memory test: 100,000 UEs on 100 radios, 256 procedures in flight

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Requests send a token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The token is either:

  • an access token, from log in, refresh the access token or initialize, valid for 15 minutes;
  • an API token, which starts with ellamocn_.

These paths take no token: GET /api/v1/livez, GET /api/v1/readyz, GET /api/v1/status, GET /api/v1/metrics, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml, POST /api/v1/init, POST /api/v1/auth/login, /refresh and /logout, and GET /api/v1/auth/oidc, /oidc/login and /oidc/callback.

items.title: Roles
items.text:
Role role_id Allows Admin 1 Everything. Read Only 2 Reading operators, radios and UE connections. Network Manager 3 Read Only, plus creating, updating and deleting operators.

Only an Admin manages users and single sign-on, and reads profiles. Every user reads its own user, changes its own password, and manages its own API tokens.

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, manage users, or update the single sign-on settings.

items.title: Responses
items.text:
Ella MOCN's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a result:

{
    "result": "Result content"
}

A failed response carries an error:

{
    "error": "Error message"
}

GET /api/v1/livez answers 204 with no body, and POST /api/v1/auth/logout too, except for a single sign-on session. GET /api/v1/readyz answers 200 when ready and 503 when not, with the same body in both cases. GET /api/v1/metrics returns text in the Prometheus exposition format, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

Times are RFC 3339, in UTC.

items.title: OpenAPI Specification
items.text:
The full API is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella MOCN instance:

GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml

items.title: Status codes
items.text:
• 200 - Success.
  • 201 - Created.
  • 204 - No content.
  • 400 - Bad request.
  • 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
  • 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
  • 404 - Not found.
  • 405 - Method not allowed.
  • 409 - Conflict.
  • 429 - Too many requests. Retry-After is the seconds to wait.
  • 500 - Internal server error.
  • 502 - The identity provider cannot be reached or used. See Update the OIDC settings.
  • 503 - Not ready. See Check readiness.

items.title: Log In
items.text:
This path returns an access token, and sets the session cookie, mocn_session, or __Host-mocn_session over TLS. The session lasts 30 days, and a user has at most 10: a new one ends the oldest.

It answers 429 Too Many Requests after 20 attempts in a minute from one client address (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64), or after 100 wrong passwords in an hour for one account.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/login

items.title: Request Body
items.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address, in any case. password string Yes Password.

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description message string Login successful. token string Access token, valid for 15 minutes.

items.title: Sample Request
items.text:
{
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "correct horse"
}

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Login successful",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

items.title: Refresh the Access Token
items.text:
This path returns a new access token for the session of the cookie.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/refresh

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description token string Access token, valid for 15 minutes.

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

items.title: Log Out
items.text:
This path ends the session of the cookie, and its access tokens, and clears the cookie. For a single sign-on session, it answers 200 with the identity provider's logout URL. Otherwise, it answers 204 with no body.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/logout

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description redirect_url string Logout URL of the identity provider.

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "redirect_url": "https://idp.example.com/realms/mocn/protocol/openid-connect/logout?client_id=mocn&post_logout_redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fmocn.example.com%2Flogin"
    }
}

items.title: Get the Single Sign-On Option
items.text:
This path returns whether single sign-on is enabled.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description enabled boolean Single sign-on is enabled. display_name string Name on the login button.

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak"
    }
}

items.title: Log In Through the Identity Provider
items.text:
This path redirects the browser to the identity provider.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/login

items.title: Query Parameters
items.text: Name In Type Description link query string 1 links the identity provider account to the user of the session cookie, and redirects to /profile, or /profile?error=<error>.

items.title: Return From the Identity Provider
items.text:
This path is the redirect URL. On success, it sets the session cookie and redirects to /. Otherwise, it redirects to /login?error=<error>.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback

items.title: Errors
items.text: Error Description rate_limited Too many logins from the address. unavailable Single sign-on is off, or the identity provider cannot be reached. failed The login expired, was already used or is invalid, the single sign-on settings changed during it, or the identity provider returned an error. denied The user or the identity provider refused access. not_set_up The identity provider gives no email, or no user has it and no group mapping is set. email_not_verified The identity provider marks the email as not verified, or does not say and trust_unverified_email is off. linked_elsewhere The user with the email is linked to another account at the identity provider. link_required The user has a password and must link the account from their profile. no_group None of the user's groups is mapped to a role. groups_overage The user is in too many groups for the identity provider to list them. too_many_users 50 users exist. error Internal error.

items.title: Initialize Ella MOCN
items.text:
This path creates the first user, an Admin, and logs it in: it returns an access token and sets the session cookie, as log in does.

Method Path POST /api/v1/init

items.title: Request Body
items.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address. ASCII letters are stored in lower case. password string Yes 8 to 72 bytes.

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description message string System initialized successfully. token string Access token, valid for 15 minutes.

items.title: Sample Request
items.text:
{
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "correct horse"
}

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "System initialized successfully",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

items.title: Get Metrics
items.text:
This path returns the metrics of the MOCN in a Prometheus exposition format negotiated from the request's Accept header: the protobuf format (application/vnd.google.protobuf, with encoding delimited, text or compact-text), or else the text format 0.0.4 (text/plain). The body is compressed with gzip when Accept-Encoding asks for it. See Observability for the list.

Method Path GET /api/v1/metrics

It answers 503 Service Unavailable when 32 requests are already in flight, or when collecting the metrics takes more than 8 seconds.

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:

# TYPE ellamocn_overload_messages_total counter
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="ng",procedure="overload_start",result="invalid"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="ng",procedure="overload_start",result="no_radio"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="ng",procedure="overload_start",result="relayed"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="ng",procedure="overload_stop",result="ignored"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="ng",procedure="overload_stop",result="invalid"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="ng",procedure="overload_stop",result="no_radio"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="ng",procedure="overload_stop",result="relayed"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="s1",procedure="overload_start",result="invalid"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="s1",procedure="overload_start",result="no_radio"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="s1",procedure="overload_start",result="relayed"} 1
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="s1",procedure="overload_stop",result="ignored"} 0
ellamocn_overload_messages_total{interface="s1",procedure="overload_stop",result="invalid"} 0

# HELP ellamocn_radio_associations Radio (eNodeB, gNodeB) associations, by interface (s1, ng) and state (connected: SCTP association up, no successful S1 or NG Setup; up: S1 or NG Setup succeeded; setup_failed: SCTP association up, Ella MOCN rejected the last S1 or NG Setup).

items.title: Get the OIDC Settings
items.text:
This path returns the OIDC settings.

Method Path GET /api/v1/oidc

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description enabled boolean Single sign-on is enabled. external_url string URL of Ella MOCN. redirect_url string Redirect URL to register at the identity provider. post_logout_redirect_url string Post-logout redirect URL to register at the identity provider. issuer string Issuer URL. client_id string Client ID. client_secret_set boolean A client secret is stored. display_name string Name on the login button. scopes array Scopes. Default 86400. trust_unverified_email boolean Accept emails without email_verified. ca_certificate string PEM CA certificates of the identity provider. ca_certificates array subject and not_after (RFC 3339) of each certificate in ca_certificate. groups_claim string Claim holding the user's groups. group_roles array group to role_id mappings. See Group Roles.

items.title: Update the OIDC Settings
items.text:
This path replaces the OIDC settings.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/oidc

items.title: Request Body
items.text: Field Type Required Description enabled boolean Yes true is refused unless the discovery document of issuer can be fetched. external_url string When enabled https URL with no path. issuer string When enabled https URL with no query or fragment. client_id string When enabled At most 255 characters. client_secret string When enabled At most 255 characters. Empty keeps the stored secret, unless issuer or client_id changes. display_name string When enabled At most 64 characters. scopes array Yes At most 20. Includes openid and email. session_lifetime_seconds int Yes 300 to 2592000. trust_unverified_email boolean No Default false. ca_certificate string No PEM certificates. groups_claim string With group_roles Claim name. group_roles array No At most 100 {group, role_id} objects. Each group at most once. role_id is 1 to 3.

items.title: Group Roles
items.text: group_roles Role at login through the identity provider Empty Set by an Admin. A user must exist. Not empty The highest role among the user's mapped groups: Admin, then Network Manager, then Read Only. A user in no mapped group is refused. A user is created if none exists. The last Admin with a password stays an Admin.

items.title: Operators
items.text: An operator is a core network that shares the radios through Ella MOCN: its PLMNs, the Global eNB ID and Global gNB ID with which Ella MOCN presents itself to its core, and its MMEs and AMFs.

items.title: List Operators
items.text:
This path returns the operators, sorted by name, with the state of their MMEs and AMFs.

Method Path GET /api/v1/operators

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description name string Name. pws_operator boolean Whether the operator's core connects the common CBC, whose warnings (PWS) are broadcast to every cell. plmns array PLMNs, each with mcc and mnc. global_enb_id object Global eNB ID that Ella MOCN uses towards the operator's MMEs. Absent when unset. global_enb_id.plmn object PLMN, with mcc and mnc. global_enb_id.enb_id_type string macro, short_macro or long_macro. global_enb_id.enb_id int eNB ID. global_gnb_id object Global gNB ID that Ella MOCN uses towards the operator's AMFs. Absent when unset. global_gnb_id.plmn object PLMN, with mcc and mnc. global_gnb_id.gnb_id int gNB ID. global_gnb_id.bit_length int gNB ID length, in bits. mmes array MMEs. Empty when none. mmes[].tnl_addresses array Addresses of the MME, reached over one SCTP association to port 36412. mmes[].status object State of the MME. See MME Status. amfs array AMFs. Empty when none. amfs[].tnl_addresses array Addresses of the AMF, reached over one SCTP association to port 38412. amfs[].status object State of the AMF. See AMF Status. user_plane.aggregation boolean Whether user traffic goes through Ella MOCN (user-plane aggregation). Always false when ran.user_plane.enabled is false in the configuration file. user_plane.status object State of the operator's user plane. See User-Plane Status. ue_connections int UE-associated logical S1-connections and NG-connections across the operator's MMEs and AMFs.

items.title: MME Status
items.text:
The state of an MME, learned from its S1 association and not stored.

Field Type Description state string disconnected: no SCTP association. connected: SCTP association up, S1 Setup not completed. up: S1 Setup succeeded. setup_failed: the MME answered S1 SETUP FAILURE. since string When the MME entered its current state. primary_tnl_address string The MME address the SCTP association sends to. Absent without an association. mme_name string MME Name from the S1 SETUP RESPONSE or MME CONFIGURATION UPDATE. Absent when the MME sent none. served_gummeis array Served GUMMEIs from the S1 SETUP RESPONSE or MME CONFIGURATION UPDATE. Absent before the S1 Setup. served_gummeis[].served_plmns array Served PLMNs, each with mcc and mnc. served_gummeis[].served_group_ids array Served MME group IDs, 0 to 65535. served_gummeis[].served_mmecs array Served MME codes, 0 to 255. relative_mme_capacity int Relative MME Capacity, 0 to 255. Absent before the S1 Setup. overload array The GUMMEIs of the MME with an ongoing overload action, from OVERLOAD START and OVERLOAD STOP. Absent when none. Cleared when the S1 association is lost. overload[].gummei object GUMMEI: plmn, mme_group_id (0 to 65535) and mme_code (0 to 255). overload[].overload_action string Overload Action from the last OVERLOAD START that applies to the GUMMEI: reject_non_emergency_mo_dt, reject_rrc_cr_signalling, permit_emergency_sessions_and_mobile_terminated_services_only, permit_high_priority_sessions_and_mobile_terminated_services_only, reject_delay_tolerant_access, permit_high_priority_sessions_and_exception_reporting_and_mobile_terminated_services_only or not_accept_mo_data_or_delay_tolerant_access_from_cp_ciot. overload[].traffic_load_reduction_indication int Traffic Load Reduction Indication from the same OVERLOAD START: the percentage of the traffic to reject, 1 to 99. Absent when the MME did not include it. ue_connections int UE-associated logical S1-connections relayed to the MME.

items.title: User-Plane Status
items.text:
The state of the operator's user plane, derived from the host's routes and not stored.

Field Type Description state string ready: Ella MOCN relays the operator's new sessions. unavailable: user-plane aggregation is on, but Ella MOCN refuses the operator's new sessions; UEs still register. off: user-plane aggregation is off for the operator. reason string Why the user plane is unavailable. Absent otherwise. not_connected: no association with the operator's MMEs or AMFs. no_route: no route to an MME or AMF. route_mismatch: the route to an MME or AMF no longer leaves by the interface its association uses, or two of them use different interfaces or addresses. no_address: the route to an MME or AMF no longer has the association's address as its source. interface_error: Ella MOCN cannot attach to the interface. too_many_operators: more operators use user-plane aggregation than Ella MOCN supports. interface string The interface the host routes the operator's MMEs and AMFs through. Absent without an association. addresses array Ella MOCN's addresses toward the operator, at most one IPv4 and one IPv6: the source addresses of its associations with the operator's MMEs and AMFs. since string When the user plane entered its current state.

items.title: AMF Status
items.text:
The state of an AMF, learned from its NG association and not stored.

Field Type Description state string disconnected: no SCTP association. connected: SCTP association up, NG Setup not completed. up: NG Setup succeeded. setup_failed: the AMF answered NG SETUP FAILURE. since string When the AMF entered its current state. primary_tnl_address string The AMF address the SCTP association sends to. Absent without an association. amf_name string AMF Name from the NG SETUP RESPONSE or AMF CONFIGURATION UPDATE. Absent before the NG Setup. served_guamis array Served GUAMI List from the NG SETUP RESPONSE or AMF CONFIGURATION UPDATE, each with plmn, amf_region_id (0 to 255), amf_set_id (0 to 1023) and amf_pointer (0 to 63). Absent before the NG Setup. plmn_support array PLMN Support List from the NG SETUP RESPONSE or AMF CONFIGURATION UPDATE. Absent before the NG Setup. plmn_support[].plmn object PLMN, with mcc and mnc. plmn_support[].snssais array S-NSSAIs, each with sst (0 to 255) and sd (6 hex digits, absent when none). relative_amf_capacity int Relative AMF Capacity, 0 to 255. Absent before the NG Setup. unavailable_guamis array GUAMIs that an AMF STATUS INDICATION marked unavailable, in the format of served_guamis. Absent when none. Cleared by NG Setup and by an AMF CONFIGURATION UPDATE with a Served GUAMI List. overload array The ongoing overload actions of the AMF, from OVERLOAD START and OVERLOAD STOP. A GUAMI is in at most one item: a later OVERLOAD START replaces the earlier one for its GUAMIs. Absent when none. Cleared by NG Setup and the loss of the NG association. overload[].guamis array GUAMI List of the OVERLOAD START, in the format of served_guamis. The served GUAMIs of the operator's PLMNs when the OVERLOAD START has no GUAMI List. overload[].overload_action string Overload Action of the AMF Overload Response: reject_non_emergency_mo_dt, reject_rrc_cr_signalling, permit_emergency_sessions_and_mobile_terminated_services_only or permit_high_priority_sessions_and_mobile_terminated_services_only. Absent when the AMF did not include it. overload[].traffic_load_reduction_indication int AMF Traffic Load Reduction Indication: the percentage of the traffic to reject, 1 to 99. Absent when the AMF did not include it. overload[].slices array Overload Start NSSAI List: each with snssais, and overload_action (Slice Overload Response) and traffic_load_reduction_indication (Slice Traffic Load Reduction Indication) when the AMF included them. Absent when none. ue_connections int UE-associated logical NG-connections relayed to the AMF.

items.title: Get an Operator

This path returns an operator, with the state of its MMEs and AMFs and its UE connections by radio.

Method Path GET /api/v1/operators/{name}

items.title: Response Fields

Absent when the radio sent none. ue_connections_by_radio[].ue_connections int UE-associated logical S1-connections or NG-connections.

items.title: Create an Operator
items.text:
This path returns the operator as Get an Operator returns it.

Method Path POST /api/v1/operators

items.title: Request Body
items.text:
Field Type Required Description name string Yes 1 to 64 characters, after leading and trailing spaces are removed. Unique. pws_operator boolean No Default false. At most one operator has true. plmns array Yes 1 to 12 PLMNs, each listed once, and owned by no other operator. Operators with MMEs have at most 32 PLMNs in total, and operators with AMFs at most 12. plmns[].mcc string Yes 3 digits. plmns[].mnc string Yes 2 or 3 digits. global_enb_id object No Absent for none. Required with mmes. global_enb_id.plmn object Yes One of plmns. global_enb_id.enb_id_type string Yes macro, short_macro or long_macro. global_enb_id.enb_id int Yes 0 to 1048575 for macro, 262143 for short_macro, 2097151 for long_macro. global_gnb_id object No Absent for none. Required with amfs. global_gnb_id.plmn object Yes One of plmns. global_gnb_id.gnb_id int Yes 0 to 2^bit_length - 1. global_gnb_id.bit_length int Yes 22 to 32. mmes array No MMEs. mmes[].tnl_addresses array Yes At least one IPv4 or IPv6 address, without a zone. An address appears at most once across the operator's MMEs. Returned in canonical form. amfs array No AMFs. amfs[].tnl_addresses array Yes At least one IPv4 or IPv6 address, without a zone. An address appears at most once across the operator's AMFs. Returned in canonical form. user_plane object No Absent for the defaults. user_plane.aggregation boolean No Default true when ran.user_plane.enabled is true in the configuration file, false otherwise. true gets 400 when it is false.

items.title: Profiling Endpoints
items.text: Method Path Description GET /api/v1/pprof/ An HTML page listing the available profiles. GET /api/v1/pprof/allocs A sampling of all past memory allocations. GET /api/v1/pprof/cmdline The command line invocation of the program. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutine Stack traces of all current goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutineleak Stack traces of all leaked goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/heap A sampling of memory allocations of live objects. GET /api/v1/pprof/profile A CPU profile, of 30 seconds by default. GET /api/v1/pprof/threadcreate Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads. GET /api/v1/pprof/trace An execution trace, of 1 second by default. GET, POST /api/v1/pprof/symbol Function names of program counters.

items.title: Query Parameters
items.text: Parameter Paths Description seconds profile, trace Duration of the capture. seconds allocs, goroutine, heap Returns the difference of the profile over this duration. debug allocs, goroutine, heap, threadcreate 0: protobuf. 1: text. 2 (goroutine): stack traces in the format of a panic. gc heap 1: runs a garbage collection first.

items.title: Radios
items.text: Radios are the eNodeBs with an S1 association and the gNodeBs with an NG association to Ella MOCN. They are learned at runtime, not stored.

items.title: List Radios
items.text:
This path returns the radios, oldest association first.

Method Path GET /api/v1/radios

items.title: Query Parameters
items.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

items.title: Response Fields
items.text:
items holds the radios of the page, page and per_page echo the query, and total_count is the number of radios. Each radio has:

Field Type Description ref string Radio identity, and the path segment that addresses it: <type>:<mcc>-<mnc>:<id>, as Ella Core names radios. See Radio Ref. Absent while the radio has no Global eNB ID or Global gNB ID, and in the setup_failed state. type string 3GPP node type: eNB over S1 or gNB over NG. global_enb_id object Global eNB ID from the S1 SETUP REQUEST. Absent for a gNB, before the radio sends one, or when Ella MOCN cannot decode it. global_enb_id.plmn object PLMN, with mcc and mnc. global_enb_id.enb_id_type string macro, home, short_macro or long_macro. global_enb_id.enb_id int eNB ID: 20 bits for macro, 28 for home, 18 for short_macro, 21 for long_macro. global_gnb_id object Global gNB ID from the NG SETUP REQUEST. Absent for an eNB, before the radio sends one, or when Ella MOCN cannot decode it. global_gnb_id.plmn object PLMN, with mcc and mnc. global_gnb_id.gnb_id int gNB ID, less than 2^bit_length. global_gnb_id.bit_length int gNB ID length, in bits: 22 to 32. name string eNB Name of an eNB, or RAN Node Name of a gNB. Absent when the radio sent none. supported_tas array Supported TAs. supported_tas[].tac string Tracking Area Code: 6 lower-case hexadecimal digits, for example 000001. The 16-bit TAC of an eNB is in the last 4 digits. supported_tas[].broadcast_plmns array Broadcast PLMNs. supported_tas[].broadcast_plmns[].plmn object PLMN, with mcc and mnc. supported_tas[].broadcast_plmns[].snssais array NG only. TAI Slice Support List of the PLMN in the tracking area: S-NSSAIs, each with sst (0 to 255) and sd (6 hex digits, absent when none). Absent for an eNB. default_paging_drx int Default paging DRX, in radio frames: 32, 64, 128 or 256. Absent before the setup. state string connected: SCTP association up, no successful S1 or NG Setup. up: S1 or NG Setup succeeded. setup_failed: SCTP association up, Ella MOCN rejected the last S1 or NG Setup. setup_failure object Last S1 or NG Setup that Ella MOCN rejected. Present in the setup_failed state only. setup_failure.cause string Cause of the S1 SETUP FAILURE or NG SETUP FAILURE, for example Unknown PLMN. setup_failure.reason string Why Ella MOCN rejected the setup, for example no operator serves a broadcast PLMN. setup_failure.at string When Ella MOCN rejected the setup. connected_at string When the SCTP association was established. tnl_addresses array Addresses of the radio. ue_connections int UE-associated logical S1-connections or NG-connections from the radio.

In the setup_failed state, global_enb_id, global_gnb_id, name, supported_tas and default_paging_drx are those of the rejected S1 SETUP REQUEST or NG SETUP REQUEST, and ue_connections is 0.

items.title: Radio Ref

items.title: Get a Radio
items.text:
This path returns a radio, with its UE connections by operator. To list its UE connections, use GET /api/v1/ue-connections?radio={ref}.

items.title: Path Parameters

items.title: Response Fields
items.text:
The fields of List Radios, plus:

Field Type Description ue_connections_by_operator array UE-associated logical S1-connections or NG-connections from the radio, by operator. Lists every operator that owns a PLMN the radio broadcasts, and every other operator with UE connections from the radio, sorted by operator name. Absent when empty. ue_connections_by_operator[].operator string Operator name. ue_connections_by_operator[].ue_connections int UE-associated logical S1-connections or NG-connections.

items.title: UE Connections
items.text: A UE connection is a UE-associated logical S1-connection or NG-connection that Ella MOCN relays between a radio and an operator's MME or AMF. UE connections are learned at runtime, not stored.

items.title: List UE Connections
items.text:
This path returns the UE connections, oldest first.

Method Path GET /api/v1/ue-connections

items.title: Query Parameters
items.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page. radio query string Only the UE connections of the radio with this ref. operator query string Only the UE connections of the operator with this name.

items.title: Response Fields
items.text:
items holds the UE connections of the page, page and per_page echo the query, and total_count is the number of UE connections that match the filters. Each UE connection has:

Field Type Description interface string s1 or ng. radio object The connection between the radio and Ella MOCN. radio.ref string The radio's ref. radio.enb_ue_s1ap_id int S1 only. eNB UE S1AP ID, allocated by the radio. 0 to 16777215. Absent until the radio answers a HANDOVER REQUEST. radio.mme_ue_s1ap_id int S1 only. MME UE S1AP ID, allocated by Ella MOCN. 0 to 4294967295. radio.ran_ue_ngap_id int NG only. RAN UE NGAP ID, allocated by the radio. 0 to 4294967295. Absent until the radio answers a HANDOVER REQUEST. radio.amf_ue_ngap_id int NG only. AMF UE NGAP ID, allocated by Ella MOCN. 0 to 1099511627775. mme object S1 only. The S1 connection between Ella MOCN and the operator's MME. mme.tnl_addresses array The MME's TNL addresses, as configured on the operator. mme.enb_ue_s1ap_id int eNB UE S1AP ID, allocated by Ella MOCN. 0 to 16777215. mme.mme_ue_s1ap_id int MME UE S1AP ID, allocated by the MME. Absent until the MME's first message for the UE. amf object NG only. The NG connection between Ella MOCN and the operator's AMF. amf.tnl_addresses array The AMF's TNL addresses, as configured on the operator. amf.ran_ue_ngap_id int RAN UE NGAP ID, allocated by Ella MOCN. 0 to 4294967295. amf.amf_ue_ngap_id int AMF UE NGAP ID, allocated by the AMF. Absent until the AMF's first message for the UE. operator string Name of the operator that serves the selected PLMN. plmn object The selected PLMN, with mcc and mnc. since string When Ella MOCN received the INITIAL UE MESSAGE, HANDOVER REQUEST or PATH SWITCH REQUEST. tai object The last TAI the radio reported for the UE: plmn and tac, 6 lower-case hexadecimal digits. Absent when none. ecgi object S1 only. The last E-UTRAN CGI the radio reported for the UE: plmn and cell_id, the 28-bit E-UTRAN Cell Identity. Absent when none. nr_cgi object NG only. The last NR CGI the radio reported for the UE: plmn and cell_id, the 36-bit NR Cell Identity. Absent when none. tunnels array With user-plane aggregation, the GTP-U tunnels Ella MOCN relays for the UE. Absent when none. tunnels[].bearer int E-RAB ID or PDU session ID. tunnels[].direction string uplink (from the radio) or downlink (from the operator). tunnels[].forwarding boolean Handover data forwarding tunnel. tunnels[].address, tunnels[].teid string, int Ella MOCN's endpoint the sender uses. tunnels[].peer_address, tunnels[].peer_teid string, int The endpoint Ella MOCN forwards to. tunnels[].packets, tunnels[].bytes int G-PDUs relayed so far, and the octets of their T-PDUs: the inner IP packet, without the GTP-U header and extension headers. End Marker and Tunnel Status messages are not counted.
