items.title: Get a User
items.text:
The email matches in any case.

Method Path GET /api/v1/users/{email}

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "email": "noc@example.com",
        "role_id": 3,
        "password_set": true,
        "oidc_linked": false
    }
}

items.title: Update a User
items.text:
This path sets the role of a user. A role change ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot change its own role, and the last Admin with a password stays an Admin. A role from group roles cannot be changed.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}

items.title: Request Body
items.text: Field Type Required Description role_id int Yes 1 to 3.

items.title: Sample Request
items.text:
{
    "role_id": 2
}

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User updated successfully"
    }
}

items.title: Update a User's Password
items.text:
This path ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot update its own password here.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}/password

items.title: Request Body
items.text: Field Type Required Description password string Yes 8 to 72 bytes.

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Password updated successfully"
    }
}

items.title: Remove a User's Password
items.text:
This path removes the password of a user, who can then log in only through the identity provider. It ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot remove its own password, and the last Admin with a password keeps it.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/password

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Password removed successfully"
    }
}

items.title: Unlink a User
items.text:
This path unlinks a user from their account at the identity provider, and ends the sessions started through it. An Admin cannot unlink itself.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/oidc

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User unlinked successfully"
    }
}

items.title: Delete a User
items.text:
This path deletes the user with its sessions and API tokens. An Admin cannot delete itself, and the last Admin with a password cannot be deleted.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User deleted successfully"
    }
}

items.title: Create an API Token
items.text:
This path returns the token, the only time it is shown. At most 12 per user. Requires an access token.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens POST /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

items.title: Request Body
items.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes 3 to 50 characters, unique among the user's tokens. expires_at string No RFC 3339 time in the future. Without it, the token does not expire.

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description token string ellamocn_, the token identifier, _ and the secret.

items.title: Sample Request
items.text:
{
    "name": "Prometheus scraper",
    "expires_at": "2027-11-13T00:00:00Z"
}

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "ellamocn_95Q0Y4lBtx2O_FAPT4VAIG3XDCT2V3D2LTEEYCS"
    }
}

items.title: List API Tokens
items.text:
This path returns the user's API tokens, oldest first.

Method Path GET /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens GET /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

items.title: Query Parameters
items.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

items.title: Response Fields
items.text: Field Type Description id string Token identifier: the part of the token between ellamocn_ and the next _. name string Name. created_at string Creation time. expires_at string Expiry time. Absent for a token that does not expire. last_used_at string Time of the last use, updated at most once a minute. Absent for a token never used.

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "95Q0Y4lBtx2O",
                "name": "Prometheus scraper",
                "created_at": "2026-11-13T16:30:39.168Z",
                "expires_at": "2027-11-13T00:00:00.000Z",
                "last_used_at": "2026-11-13T16:30:55.267Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

items.title: Delete an API Token
items.text: Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens/{id} DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens/{id}

items.title: Sample Response
items.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "API token deleted successfully"
    }
}

items.title: Tutorials
items.text:
These tutorials are a hands-on introduction to Ella MOCN.

  • Connect Your First Radio

items.title: Connect Your First Radio
items.text:
In this tutorial, we will run two operators' 4G cores and Ella MOCN on one machine, connect a 4G radio to Ella MOCN, and attach a phone of each operator to its own core through that radio. Ella Core is the core of both operators.

You can expect to spend about 30 minutes completing this tutorial.

items.title: Pre-requisites
items.text:
To complete this tutorial, you will need:

  • A Linux machine with Docker installed, and an Ethernet port, eth1, connected to the radio.
  • A 4G radio (eNB) that can broadcast two PLMNs.
  • Two phones, with SIM cards programmed with these values:
Phone IMSI Key OPc Operator A's phone 001010000000001 465b5ce8b199b49faa5f0a2ee238a6bc cd63cb71954a9f4e48a5994e37a02baf Operator B's phone 001020000000001 465b5ce8b199b49faa5f0a2ee238a6bc cd63cb71954a9f4e48a5994e37a02baf

items.title: 1. Write the Compose File
items.text:
Create a new directory for this tutorial and navigate into it:

mkdir ella-mocn-tutorial
cd ella-mocn-tutorial

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml
configs:
  ella_core_a_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        system:
          level: "info"
          output: "stdout"
        audit:
          output: "stdout"
      db:
        path: "/data/core.db"
      interfaces:
        n2:
          address: "192.168.10.2"
        n3:
          name: "n3"
        n6:
          name: "eth0"
        api:
          address: "0.0.0.0"
          port: 5002
      datapath:
        attach-mode: "tcx"
  ella_core_b_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        system:
          level: "info"
          output: "stdout"
        audit:
          output: "stdout"
      db:
        path: "/data/core.db"
      interfaces:
        n2:
          address: "192.168.10.5"
        n3:
          name: "n3"
        n6:
          name: "eth0"
        api:
          address: "0.0.0.0"
          port: 5002
      datapath:
        attach-mode: "tcx"
  ella_mocn_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/mocn.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5030
      ran:
        signalling:
          address: 0.0.0.0
          s1_port: 36412

services:
  ella-core-a:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-core:v1.22.0
    configs:
      - source: ella_core_a_config
        target: /core.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/core --config /core.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    privileged: true
    volumes:
      - ella-core-a-data:/data
    ports:
      - "5002:5002"
    networks:
      default:
        driver_opts:
          com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: eth0
      ran:
        driver_opts:
          com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: n3
        ipv4_address: 192.168.10.2

  ella-core-b:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-core:v1.22.0
    configs:
      - source: ella_core_b_config
        target: /core.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/core --config /core.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    privileged: true
    volumes:
      - ella-core-b-data:/data
    ports:
      - "5003:5002"
    networks:
      default:
        driver_opts:
          com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: eth0
      ran:
        driver_opts:
          com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: n3
        ipv4_address: 192.168.10.5

  ella-mocn:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-mocn:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_mocn_config
        target: /mocn.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/mocn --config /mocn.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ella-mocn-data:/data
    ports:
      - "5030:5030"
    networks:
      default: {}
      ran:
        ipv4_address: 192.168.10.3

networks:
  ran:
    driver: macvlan
    driver_opts:
      parent: eth1
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 192.168.10.0/24

volumes:
  ella-core-a-data:
  ella-core-b-data:
  ella-mocn-data:

The radio reaches Ella MOCN at 192.168.10.3, Operator A's core at 192.168.10.2 and Operator B's core at 192.168.10.5, on eth1.

items.title: 2. Start Ella Core and Ella MOCN
items.text:
Start the containers:

docker compose up -d

You should see the following output:

 ✔ Network ella-mocn-tutorial_default            Created
 ✔ Network ella-mocn-tutorial_ran                Created
 ✔ Volume ella-mocn-tutorial_ella-core-a-data    Created
 ✔ Volume ella-mocn-tutorial_ella-core-b-data    Created
 ✔ Volume ella-mocn-tutorial_ella-mocn-data      Created
 ✔ Container ella-mocn-tutorial-ella-mocn-1      Started
 ✔ Container ella-mocn-tutorial-ella-core-b-1    Started
 ✔ Container ella-mocn-tutorial-ella-core-a-1    Started

items.title: 3. Configure Operator A's Core
items.text:
Open your browser at http://127.0.0.1:5002/. The Initialize Ella Core page opens.

Create the first user with the following credentials, and click Create:

  • Email: admin@ellanetworks.com
  • Password: admin

The Ella Core dashboard opens.

Go to Operator. Operator ID (MCC/MNC) is 001 / 01 and Supported TACs is 000001(1).

Go to Subscribers and click Create. Create a subscriber with the following parameters:

  • IMSI: 0000000001, after the 00101 prefix.
  • Key: 465b5ce8b199b49faa5f0a2ee238a6bc
  • Sequence Number: keep the default value.
  • Profile: keep the default value, default.
  • Select Provide custom OPC and set OPC (optional) to cd63cb71954a9f4e48a5994e37a02baf.

Click Create. The subscriber 001010000000001 appears with the status Deregistered.

items.title: 4. Configure Operator B's Core
items.text:
Open your browser at http://127.0.0.1:5003/ and create the first user with the same credentials as in step 3.

Go to Operator. Next to Operator ID (MCC/MNC), click the edit icon, set MNC to 02 and click Update. Operator ID (MCC/MNC) shows 001 / 02.

Go to Subscribers and create a subscriber with the same parameters as in step 3. The IMSI prefix is now 00102, and the subscriber 001020000000001 appears with the status Deregistered.

items.title: 5. Initialize Ella MOCN
items.text:
Open your browser at http://127.0.0.1:5030/. The Initialize Ella MOCN page opens.

Create the first user with the following credentials, and click Create:

  • Email: admin@ellanetworks.com
  • Password: adminadmin

The Ella MOCN dashboard opens.

items.title: 6. Create the Operators
items.text:
Go to Operators and click Create. Set:

  • Name: Operator A
  • MCC: 001
  • MNC: 01

Click Create. The Operators / Operator A page opens.

Next to 4G Gateway Identity (Global eNB ID), click the edit icon. Turn on Set a Global eNB ID and set eNB ID to 1. Keep PLMN at 001-01 and eNB ID type at Macro (20 bits). Click Save.

4G Gateway Identity (Global eNB ID) shows 001-01 · Macro (20 bits) · 1.

In Core Network Nodes, click Add Core Node. Keep Type at MME (4G), set Address 1 to 192.168.10.2, Operator A's core, and click Add. The MME appears with the status Connected. It stays Connected until a radio connects.

Go back to Operators and create Operator B the same way, with:

  • MNC: 02
  • eNB ID: 1, with PLMN 001-02
  • MME address: 192.168.10.5, Operator B's core

items.title: 7. Connect the Radio
items.text:
In your radio's configuration, set:

  • IP address: 192.168.10.10/24, on the port connected to eth1
  • MME address: 192.168.10.3, Ella MOCN
  • PLMNs: 001-01 and 001-02
  • TAC: 1

Restart the radio if its configuration requires it.

In the Ella MOCN UI, go to Radios. Your radio appears with the status Up.

Go to Operators. In Core Network Nodes, both operators show 1/1 up.

items.title: 8. Attach the Phones
items.text:
Insert the SIM cards and turn on both phones. On each phone, set the APN to internet.

In the Ella MOCN UI, go to Radios and click your radio. Under UE Connections by Operator, Operator A and Operator B each have 1 UE connection.

Go to Operators and click Operator B. In Core Network Nodes, the MME has the name ella, the status Up and 1 UE connection.

Both phones are attached to their own operator's core through the same radio.

items.title: Clean Up
items.text:
Stop and remove the containers, networks and volumes:

docker compose down -v
